You'll gain expertise in data visualization, machine learning, statistical modeling, and database management, making you a highly marketable professional in the rapidly growing field of data analytics.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Applied Analytics

description: The M.S. in Interdisciplinary Studies is a graduate degree option designed to allow students, in consultation with faculty, to develop a unique program of study for their master's degree. Students are encouraged to pursue an interdisciplinary approach to learning by taking courses in three distinct academic disciplines, forming an overarching degree plan that is centered around a specific topic or field of interest. Students are admitted to the program under one of several designated specializations. With prior approval, students may develop a new specialization to meet their academic and professional goals.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Computational Linguistics

description: The Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies (MSIS) is a research-intensive graduate degree that encourages the integration of knowledge from two or more academic disciplines. The MSIS is housed in the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences and designed to foster interdisciplinary learning under the guidance of a graduate faculty advisor and a supervisory committee. Students pursue individualized course plans based on their academic and research interests and develop an interdisciplinary thesis (3 credit hours) or project (0 credit hours). This particular program of study combines coursework from the College of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences (specifically, the Department of Media Arts) and the Mayborn College of Health and Public Affairs (specifically, the Department of Public Administration). This particular program of study (MSIS with a concentration in Digital Communication Analytics) is a professional master's degree that prepares students for careers as digital communication analysts, researchers, strategists, and managers in a variety of public, private, and non-profit organizations. Students gain expertise in data collection, analysis, visualization, and storytelling to inform strategic communication decisions in a data-driven environment.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Digital Communication Analytics
Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Geographic Information Systems (GIS)

description: The Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies (MSIS) with a concentration in Geospatial Intelligence (GSI) is a 36-credit-hour program designed to equip students with a robust skillset in geographic information science, remote sensing, and intelligence analysis techniques. Graduates will be prepared for a variety of careers in government, industry, and academia, focusing on the collection, analysis, and dissemination of geospatial information to support decision-making.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Geospatial Intelligence

description: The Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Health Data Analytics offers students the foundational knowledge and skills needed to address the complex challenges of the healthcare industry through data analysis. This program is designed to integrate various fields — computer science, statistics, public health, information science, and other areas — to prepare students for careers in the rapidly growing health data analytics field. Students learn to collect, manage, analyze, and interpret large health care data sets, apply statistical and machine learning techniques, and communicate findings effectively to inform decision-making in clinical, administrative and research settings. Students also gain practical experience through projects and case studies, equipping them with the ability to transform raw data into actionable insights for improving patient care, public health outcomes and health system efficiency.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Health Data Analytics

description: The M.S. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Instructional Systems Design (ISD) prepares you to be a leader, practitioner, or researcher in the field of learning and development. This program allows you to customize your learning with courses from other disciplines related to your interests and career goals. Instructional systems designers are in demand in corporations, government, military, K-12, higher education, and healthcare. If you want to make a difference in how people learn and perform, this program is for you. Graduates of this program will be equipped with the knowledge and skills to lead in the transformation of learning and development. This is a 30-hour program with a variety of course delivery options, including online, face-to-face, or blended. The ISD program offers a non-thesis option, which requires completion of a comprehensive exam, as well as a thesis option. The thesis option allows you to conduct research on a topic of interest, under the direction of a faculty member, and to present your findings in a written thesis. The thesis option is required for students who wish to pursue a doctoral degree.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Instructional Systems Design

description: The M.S. in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Workforce Leadership and Development provides students with the opportunity to pursue an individualized, interdisciplinary course of study designed to meet their specific career and educational goals while focusing on the knowledge and skills necessary for leadership in various workforce and organizational settings. Students will gain advanced knowledge and skills in areas such as organizational development, human resource management, training and development, and leadership theory and practice, preparing them for roles in corporate, non-profit, government, and educational sectors. The program is designed to develop critical thinkers and ethical leaders who can effectively address the complex challenges of modern workforces.
Program name: Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Workforce Leadership and Development

description: The M.S. in International Sustainable Tourism is an interdisciplinary program that develops in-depth knowledge of sustainable tourism planning and development. The program provides a comprehensive understanding of sustainable tourism to help students: Become leaders in sustainable tourism development and policy creation. Analyze and address tourism challenges at local, national and international levels. Create and implement effective sustainable tourism solutions. Collaborate with stakeholders to promote responsible tourism practices. Contribute to the economic, social and environmental well-being of destinations worldwide. The curriculum encompasses core subjects such as tourism geography, cultural heritage management, environmental policy, and sustainable hospitality operations. Elective courses allow for specialization in areas such as ecotourism, community-based tourism, and destination marketing. The program culminates in a thesis or professional project, enabling students to apply their knowledge to real-world challenges.
Program name: Master of Science in International Sustainable Tourism

Concentration name: Exercise Physiology, Sport and Exercise Psychology
description: The Master of Science in Kinesiology degree prepares students for advanced study and professional careers in fields such as exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor control, and sport and exercise psychology. This program has an emphasis on exercise science, with a focus on human movement and its impact on health and performance. The program provides the theoretical and practical knowledge base for students seeking careers in academic, clinical, and applied settings. Students will learn how to design, conduct, and interpret research in various areas of kinesiology, preparing them for doctoral studies or research-oriented careers. Graduates will be equipped to work in areas such as cardiovascular fitness, exercise prescription, strength and conditioning, sports performance, and health promotion.
Program name: Master of Science in Kinesiology

description: The Department of Learning Technologies provides an intensive program of study in the Master of Science (M.S.) in Learning Technologies. The department has been one of the pioneering programs in the country to focus on the impact of technology on education and training through the study of human learning and development, design of technology-based learning experiences, and effective integration of technology in various learning contexts. The program provides the knowledge, skills, and dispositions necessary to design, develop, implement, and evaluate effective learning environments and experiences in various contexts. The coursework provides students with a strong theoretical foundation in learning, instructional design, and human performance improvement, and practical skills in instructional technology. The graduates of the program are able to apply appropriate research and evaluation methods to improve learning and performance.
Program name: Master of Science in Learning Technologies

Concentration name: Archival Studies, Digital Content and Information, Information Organization, Law Librarianship, Music Librarianship, Youth Services, Generalist (design your own)
description: The Master of Science in Library Science (MSLS) degree program at the University of North Texas prepares students for careers as information professionals in libraries and other information environments. This 36-semester credit hour program emphasizes professional education in theory and practice across the information landscape. Students learn to organize, manage, and disseminate information in diverse formats and for diverse audiences. The MSLS degree prepares students to serve as leaders and innovators in an evolving information society. With an emphasis on information literacy, access, and service, the MSLS program ensures graduates are well-equipped to address the challenges and opportunities of the 21st century information professional. Students are encouraged to pursue an area of specialization based on their career interests. Possible specializations include archival studies, digital content and information, information organization, law librarianship, music librarianship, and youth services. A generalist option is also available.
Accreditation status: The Master of Science in Library Science (MSLS) degree program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA).
Program name: Master of Science in Library Science

description: The Master of Science in Library Science (M.S.) degree program at UNT prepares students for professional careers in diverse information environments. Our program helps students develop the knowledge, skills, and ethical values necessary to manage, organize, and provide access to information resources and services. Graduates of the program are equipped to contribute to the advancement of library and information science in a rapidly changing world.
Accreditation status: The Master of Science in Library Science (M.S.) degree program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA).
Program name: Master of Science in Library Science with a concentration in Archival Studies

description: The Master of Science in Library Science (MSLS) degree is designed for those who want to prepare for careers as information professionals in the evolving information environment of the 21st century. The program focuses on the management, organization, preservation, and retrieval of information and knowledge, as well as on leadership and services in libraries and other information agencies. The coursework provides students with the foundational principles and practices of the library and information professions. The program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA), the national accrediting agency for master’s programs in library and information science in the United States and Canada. Students in this program are eligible for multiple specializations that include Archives and Records Management, Children's and Young Adult Librarianship, Information Organization, Law Librarianship, Music Librarianship and School Librarianship.
Accreditation status: The program is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA), the national accrediting agency for master’s programs in library and information science in the United States and Canada.
Program name: Master of Science in Library Science with a concentration in Children's and Young Adult Librarianship

description: The Master of Science in Library Science (M.S.) program prepares students for careers as information professionals in libraries and other information organizations. Our program helps students develop the knowledge, skills, and dispositions to provide leadership in the rapidly changing information environment. The Information Organization concentration focuses on the theory and practice of organizing and representing information in various formats. Students learn about cataloging, classification, metadata, and information architecture, preparing them for roles in information description and discovery across a range of settings.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Library Association (ALA)
Program name: Master of Science in Library Science with a concentration in Information Organization

description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Library Science prepares students for professional careers in libraries and other information agencies. Students completing this degree will develop a strong foundation of knowledge and skills in the principles and practices of library and information science. The program’s curriculum is flexible, with options for students to specialize in a particular area of library and information science through our concentrations. The program also offers students the ability to complete the degree online.
Accreditation status: The UNT M.S. in Library Science is accredited by the American Library Association (ALA).
Program name: Master of Science in Library Science with a concentration in Knowledge Management

description: The concentration in Law Librarianship and Legal Informatics prepares students for professional careers in academic law libraries, court libraries, law firm libraries, government law libraries, and other legal information environments. Students learn legal research skills, legal information management, and the principles of intellectual property, copyright, legal technology, and legal informatics. The program emphasizes an understanding of the legal system and how information professionals support legal practice and research. The concentration prepares students to lead and innovate in the evolving landscape of legal information and technology.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Library Association (ALA), 225 N. Michigan Ave., Suite 1300, Chicago, IL 60601.
Program name: Master of Science in Library Science with a concentration in Law Librarianship and Legal Informatics

description: The Department of Linguistics offers a Master of Science degree in Linguistics. This degree program is designed to provide graduate training in linguistic analysis and theory, as well as in the various subfields of linguistics. Our program offers excellent training in core linguistic areas and in more specialized areas such as computational linguistics, field linguistics, and language documentation, second language acquisition, and corpus linguistics. As a graduate student, you will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty mentors, develop your own research interests, and contribute to the vibrant intellectual life of our department.
Program name: Master of Science in Linguistics

description: The Master of Science in Interdisciplinary Studies with a concentration in Computational Linguistics (M.S.) focuses on a multidisciplinary approach to the automatic processing of human language, drawing on the fields of linguistics, computer science, and library and information sciences. Students receive a thorough grounding in all aspects of linguistic science and computational analysis as it applies to natural language. Students will become familiar with current trends in computational linguistics and apply computational linguistic techniques in courses within the Department of Linguistics, the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, and the Department of Information Science. Additionally, students gain experience with a wide variety of tools and methodologies and develop the skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate solutions for a wide range of problems involving natural language. The program prepares students for careers in industry (e.g., text analytics, natural language processing, data science, language technology development) and for continued graduate study at the doctoral level.
Program name: Master of Science in Linguistics with a concentration in Computational Linguistics

description: The MS in Linguistics at UNT is designed for students interested in careers where advanced linguistic knowledge is required. The program prepares students for positions in government, NGOs, and industry that require linguistic training. Students completing the MS can also use this degree to springboard to other professional programs (e.g., law, computational linguistics, language documentation). The concentration in English as a Second Language (ESL) is ideal for those planning to teach ESL in the US or abroad, or for those who wish to pursue careers in ESL material development or curriculum design. The ESL concentration provides students with theoretical and practical training for careers as ESL teachers and specialists. Our program prepares students for positions in public and private language institutes, adult education programs, and community colleges.
Program name: Master of Science in Linguistics with a concentration in English as a Second Language (ESL)

description: The Department of Linguistics offers both a Master of Arts (M.A.) and a Master of Science (M.S.) in Linguistics. Within the M.A. and M.S. degrees, students can choose to pursue concentrations in Computational Linguistics, Language Documentation, or TESOL. The M.A. degree provides students with a broad knowledge of language and linguistics and prepares them to teach English as a second language, teach linguistics at a community college, or pursue further graduate work in linguistics. The M.S. degree is similar to the M.A., but it also provides students with a stronger background in quantitative methods and prepares them for careers in language-related industries, such as computational linguistics, natural language processing, or language documentation. Students are required to take a set of core courses, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Students will also complete a capstone project that allows them to apply their knowledge to a real-world problem or research question. The M.A. and M.S. in Linguistics degrees are designed to provide students with a strong foundation in linguistic theory and methods, as well as opportunities for specialized study in areas such as computational linguistics, language documentation, and TESOL. Students will develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills, preparing them for diverse careers or further academic pursuits.
Program name: Master of Science in Linguistics with a concentration in Language Documentation

description:
The MS in Materials Science and Engineering is designed to prepare graduates to fill important industry and research needs. Students will focus on developing advanced knowledge and skills in the processing, structure, properties, and performance of materials, as well as the relationships between these elements. Our graduates will be able to apply advanced materials science and engineering principles to solve problems, develop new materials, and advance technologies in various fields.
The MS in Materials Science and Engineering prepares students for careers in research and development, materials production, process engineering, quality control, and management in industries such as aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and biomedical. The program provides a strong foundation for those who wish to pursue a Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering or related fields.
Program name: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The Master of Science degree in mathematics is designed to provide students with advanced training in mathematics, either as preparation for doctoral studies in mathematics or for careers in industry, government, or teaching in community colleges. Students may elect a thesis option or a non-thesis option. The thesis option provides research experience under the supervision of a faculty member.
Program name: Master of Science in Mathematics

description: The Mathematics Education Concentration is designed for students who want to continue their study of mathematics and mathematics education beyond the undergraduate level. The program is specifically designed to prepare students for teaching mathematics in high schools and community colleges, for positions as mathematics specialists, and for further graduate study in mathematics education at the doctoral level. Students will gain advanced knowledge in a variety of mathematical topics. In addition, students will learn to apply research-based pedagogical content knowledge in teaching mathematics effectively. They will also learn about current issues, trends and research in mathematics education. Our graduate courses are offered in a flexible format, with opportunities for students to study face-to-face, online or in a blended fashion. Many of our courses are offered at convenient evening hours, making it possible for students who work full-time to complete the program. Students may complete the degree entirely online as well.
Program name: Master of Science in Mathematics with a Concentration in Mathematics Education

description: The Mechanical and Energy Engineering Department offers graduate study leading to the Master of Science (MS) in Mechanical and Energy Engineering. The MS program offers thesis and non-thesis options. The MS program focuses on advanced topics in Mechanical and Energy Engineering and prepares students for careers in industry, government, or academia. Students can specialize in areas such as materials and manufacturing, thermal-fluid sciences, dynamics and controls, and energy systems. The program provides a strong theoretical foundation coupled with practical applications and research opportunities. Graduates will be equipped to tackle complex engineering challenges and contribute to innovative solutions in their chosen fields.
Program name: Master of Science in Mechanical and Energy Engineering

description: The Master of Science in Merchandising and Consumer Analytics is designed to prepare students for leadership and management careers in the dynamic, global merchandising industry. The program provides advanced knowledge and skills in merchandising and consumer analytics with a focus on problem solving, strategic planning, decision making, and consumer behavior analysis. This program aims to develop individuals into strategic thinkers and leaders who can leverage data to make informed business decisions in merchandising. Students will learn how to analyze consumer behavior, market trends, and retail data to develop effective merchandising strategies. The curriculum integrates theoretical knowledge with practical applications, preparing graduates to excel in diverse roles within the retail, fashion, and consumer goods sectors.
Program name: Master of Science in Merchandising and Consumer Analytics

description: The Department of Merchandising and Digital Retailing in the College of Merchandising, Hospitality and Tourism offers the Master of Science (M.S.) degree program in Merchandising and Digital Retailing with a major in Merchandising and Digital Retailing. This program prepares graduates for careers in merchandising, retail management, supply chain management, and digital retailing through courses in merchandising, retail analytics, technology, and global supply chain management. Graduates are prepared for careers in merchandising, retail management, supply chain management and digital retailing, as well as for doctoral study. A thesis option is available.
Program name: Master of Science in Merchandising and Digital Retailing

description: The M.S. in Physics program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in experimental, computational or theoretical physics while pursuing advanced coursework. This degree prepares students for doctoral study or a career in industry. Students choose a thesis or non-thesis option and may pursue various fields of study including, but not limited to, Accelerator Physics, Astrophysics, Biophysics, Condensed Matter Physics, Materials Science, Medical Physics, and Optics.
Program name: Master of Science in Physics

description: The Professional Science Master’s (PSM) option in Biology, administered by the Department of Biological Sciences, combines advanced biological sciences training with marketable skills in the areas of business, communication, and project management to prepare students for leadership roles in science-related professions. The program emphasizes an internship-based, problem-solving approach to develop professionals with the scientific knowledge and business acumen to succeed in the workplace. This program is offered to students who hold a bachelor’s degree in a science field or a related area.
Program name: Master of Science in Professional Science Master's degree option (biology)

description: The Professional Science Master's (PSM) degree option with a major in Chemistry is a non-thesis, interdisciplinary master's degree program designed to provide students with advanced training in chemistry while simultaneously developing highly valued business and professional skills required for successful careers in industrial or governmental settings. The PSM program is designed to meet the growing need for talented scientists who also possess professional skills in communication, management, and regulatory affairs.
Program name: Master of Science in Professional Science Master's degree option (chemistry)

description: The Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling program at the University of North Texas prepares graduates to work with individuals with disabilities and chronic illnesses. Graduates work as rehabilitation counselors in a variety of public and private settings, including state and federal vocational rehabilitation agencies, community rehabilitation programs, hospitals, mental health programs, supported employment programs, private practice, and insurance companies. This online program will equip you with the skills to address the social, psychological, and vocational impact of disabilities on individuals and their families. Throughout the UNT M.S. in Rehabilitation Counseling program, you will develop a deep understanding of disabilities and their impact, as well as the counseling techniques to support individuals in achieving their goals. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including: Disability and rehabilitation, Counseling theories and techniques, Assessment and evaluation, Vocational rehabilitation, Case management, Ethical and legal issues in rehabilitation, Group counseling, Family counseling, Career development, Research and program evaluation.
Accreditation status: The Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling program is accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP).
Program name: Master of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling

description: The Master of Science (MS) program in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering (SME) is designed to educate students on fundamental principles and knowledge pertaining to semiconductor manufacturing process integration, device and circuit design, and manufacturing and industrial engineering. Students will gain knowledge in semiconductor manufacturing processes, semiconductor device physics, process control, cleanroom operations, testing and reliability, and the economics of manufacturing, and will learn to apply these principles to solve complex problems in the semiconductor industry. The semiconductor manufacturing industry has been expanding at a rapid pace and is expected to continue this growth for decades. The US CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 provides billions in funding for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and R&D, creating a need for a highly skilled workforce across the entire supply chain. Graduates of this program will be prepared to fill critical roles in semiconductor manufacturing, research and development, and management within the semiconductor industry, contributing to the economic growth of the DFW metroplex, the state of Texas, and the nation.
Program name: Master of Science in Semiconductor Manufacturing Engineering

Concentration name: Direct Practice with Families and Children, Administrative and Community Practice
description: The Master of Science in Social Work (MSW) program at the University of North Texas is a nationally accredited program designed to prepare students for advanced social work practice. The UNT MSW Program is a generalist curriculum with concentrations in Direct Practice with Families and Children, and Administrative and Community Practice. The program offers face-to-face and online options. Students can enroll full-time or part-time. The program prepares students for leadership in multiple practice settings. MSW graduates may choose to become licensed social workers in Texas (LMSW and LCSW).
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE)
Program name: Master of Science in Social Work (MSW)

description: The Department of Sociology offers the Master of Science degree in Sociology. The M.S. program is designed to provide advanced training in sociological theory, research methods, and statistics. It prepares students for a variety of professional positions, including research analysts, data scientists, policy analysts, program evaluators, and administrators in government, non-profit organizations, and the private sector. The M.S. degree also serves as excellent preparation for students who wish to pursue a Ph.D. in sociology or a related social science field.
Program name: Master of Science in Sociology

description: The Department of Speech and Hearing Sciences offers a Master of Science degree program in Speech-Language Pathology that is designed to prepare students to practice as speech-language pathologists. The program requires 57 credit hours of graduate course work beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students are typically full-time and graduate within two years after beginning graduate-level courses. Our graduates work in a variety of settings, including public schools, hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and private practices. After completing the MS degree, students are eligible to apply for Texas state licensure and national certification from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). Students who do not have an undergraduate degree in communication sciences and disorders may be admitted into the program. These students must complete undergraduate prerequisites prior to beginning graduate-level courses. These prerequisites can be completed at UNT as a post-baccalaureate student or at another university. If you have questions about prerequisites, please email us at shs-advising@unt.edu.
Accreditation status: The Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology program at UNT is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA), 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700. Our program meets the educational requirements for the Speech-Language Pathologist license in Texas.
Program name: Master of Science in Speech-Language Pathology

description: The Master of Science (MS) in Taxation and Data Analytics is designed to prepare students for professional careers in taxation using data analytics. This program will develop skills in the areas of tax planning, tax compliance, tax research, tax technology and data analytics. This includes developing and interpreting data models, data visualization, and the ability to apply current and emerging data analytic techniques to solve taxation problems. This program combines both tax and data analytics courses within the G. Brint Ryan College of Business and the College of Engineering. Upon completion of this program, students will be prepared for careers in public accounting, corporate taxation, and governmental agencies, and will be able to sit for the CPA exam in Texas.
Program name: Master of Science in Taxation and Data Analytics

description: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at the University of North Texas is a four-year clinical doctorate designed to prepare students for professional practice in audiology. The curriculum meets the academic and clinical requirements for licensure as an audiologist in Texas and for national certification by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). The program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences related to hearing and balance, as well as extensive clinical training in all areas of audiology. Students complete a minimum of 75 semester credit hours of academic coursework and 2000 hours of supervised clinical experience, including a full-time externship during the fourth year. Our students gain clinical experience in a variety of specialty areas including cochlear implants, pediatrics, educational audiology, and private practice settings. Students also have the opportunity to engage in research across a wide range of interests including electrophysiology, psychoacoustics, speech perception, hearing aids, and vestibular assessment. The UNT Au.D. program is committed to excellence in education, research, and clinical practice, preparing students to be leaders in the field of audiology.
Accreditation status: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) program at the University of North Texas is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
Program name: Doctor of Audiology (AuD)

description: The Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) is a professional doctorate designed for senior managers and executives seeking to apply advanced academic theory and rigorous research to practical business problems. Unlike a Ph.D. program, which primarily prepares graduates for academic research careers, the DBA focuses on developing scholar-practitioners who can bridge the gap between academic theory and real-world business challenges. The UNT DBA program emphasizes research that directly contributes to business practice, policy, and strategy. Our graduates are equipped to lead organizational change, innovate business models, and address complex problems with data-driven insights. They often pursue roles in senior management, consulting, or specialized research within corporations, government, or non-profit organizations.
Accreditation status: AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (for the G. Brint Ryan College of Business)
Program name: Doctor of Business Administration (DBA)

description: The DMA in Performance is the most advanced music performance degree offered at UNT, preparing students for careers as performing musicians and artist-teachers at the highest level. Students develop expertise in their principal applied area of study, gaining a breadth of knowledge across music history, theory, and literature, and a deep understanding of repertoire. Throughout the program, students refine their musical and technical skills, interpretative abilities, and scholarly research while developing a distinctive artistic voice. Opportunities abound for students to perform as soloists, in chamber ensembles, and in large ensembles in a wide range of styles, genres, and historical periods. Students receive intensive private instruction, participate in master classes, and have access to UNT’s world-class facilities and performance venues. Upon completion of the DMA in Performance, students will be prepared to assume positions in college/university music departments, professional symphony orchestras, opera companies, touring ensembles, and other performance venues.
Program name: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Performance

description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Art Education at the University of North Texas provides an advanced course of study that is focused on art education as a broad field of inquiry and practice, including, but not limited to, K-12 schooling contexts, post-secondary education, museums and community arts organizations. The curriculum is designed to educate scholars who will contribute to research, theory, policy and practice in art education locally, nationally and globally.

The faculty members in the Department of Art Education and Art History are active researchers, practitioners and educators whose work reflects an extensive range of approaches to research, diverse theoretical and methodological perspectives, and varied areas of emphasis related to learning and teaching in art. Faculty interests include critical studies, social justice, curriculum development, culturally responsive pedagogy, teacher education, community art education, visual culture, disability studies, and contemporary art practices in education. Students are encouraged to pursue an individualized course of study that aligns with their intellectual interests and professional aspirations within the broad scope of the field of art education. The program emphasizes both disciplinary breadth and individualized depth through a flexible curriculum of foundational studies, advanced seminars and independent research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Art Education

Concentration name: Basic Behavior Analysis, Applied Behavior Analysis
description: Doctoral students in Behavioral Science are trained in the experimental analysis of behavior, applied behavior analysis, and behavioral neuroscience. Students are expected to conduct original research that advances the basic science of behavior and/or addresses socially significant problems. Our doctoral program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for careers in academia, research, or practice. Many of our graduates become university professors, researchers, or clinical practitioners. The program emphasizes a strong foundation in research methodology, experimental design, and quantitative analysis, preparing students to be leaders in the field.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Behavioral Science

description: The Biochemistry and Molecular Biology Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with a strong background in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, genetics, and bioinformatics. The interdisciplinary nature of the program offers students the opportunity to conduct research in diverse areas, including: Protein structure and function; Enzymology and metabolism; Gene regulation and epigenetics; Cell signaling and communication; Neurobiology and development; Cancer biology; Infectious disease; Biotechnology and synthetic biology; Bioinformatics and computational biology. Our faculty members are highly collaborative and committed to mentoring students in both experimental and theoretical approaches. Students gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge techniques and instrumentation, preparing them for successful careers in academia, industry, and government. The program culminates in the completion and defense of a doctoral dissertation based on original research.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology

description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Biology. Our graduate students are fully integrated into research activities and benefit from state-of-the-art facilities and instrumentation, strong faculty mentoring and abundant research and teaching assistantships. Students pursue research in areas ranging from ecology, evolutionary biology and behavior to environmental science and toxicology to cell and molecular biology and physiology. Our students are well-prepared for careers in academia, industry and government agencies.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology

description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers graduate work leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology. The PhD program offers advanced study and research in a variety of areas of biological sciences. Admission to the PhD program is contingent upon approval of the faculty and the chair of the department. The PhD program is a research degree and requires a minimum of 60 semester hours (36 semester hours of course work and 24 semester hours of dissertation). The department offers concentrations in biochemistry, cell biology, ecology, environmental sciences, genetics, microbiology, physiology and plant sciences.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biology with a concentration in Exercise Physiology

description: Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. students work in research laboratories focusing on understanding and solving biomedical problems related to human health. Students enrolled in the Ph.D. program in Biomedical Engineering will take a set of core courses and then pursue advanced coursework and research in a chosen area of specialization. This program prepares students for careers in academia, industrial research and development, and government research laboratories.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Biomedical Engineering

Concentration name: Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Logistics and Supply Chain Management, Marketing, Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management, Strategic Management
description:
A Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Business from the G. Brint Ryan College of Business at the University of North Texas prepares you for a career as a university professor and researcher. As a student in the program, you will develop expertise in research methods and theories, and learn how to conduct independent and original research. You will learn how to produce high-quality scholarly research in your primary concentration, enabling you to contribute to knowledge generation and dissemination. A Ph.D. in Business from UNT enables you to make a significant impact on your field of study. Upon graduating, you will be prepared for a career at a research-intensive institution as a tenure-track faculty member. Our graduates typically find placements at AACSB-accredited business schools in the U.S. and around the world.

Admission to the program is highly selective, and applicants are expected to have an outstanding academic record, competitive GRE or GMAT scores, strong letters of recommendation, and a demonstrated interest in pursuing academic research. The program is full-time, requiring a significant commitment of time and effort over four to five years to complete. Students are required to take 69 credit hours for the PhD. After the first year, students can apply for an in-residence master’s degree, which usually requires them to take 30 credits to meet the requirements of the master's degree. Students are typically provided with financial support, which includes a stipend and tuition waiver, in exchange for working as a teaching or research assistant. The financial support package also typically includes health insurance.

To learn more about individual concentrations and their requirements, please visit the G. Brint Ryan College of Business website.
Accreditation status: The G. Brint Ryan College of Business is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB Accreditation is the hallmark of excellence in business education, and has been earned by less than five percent of the world’s business programs.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Business

description: UNT’s Ph.D. in Chemistry program is designed to develop students into independent, creative and responsible researchers in the chemical sciences. It offers coursework and research opportunities in all major areas of chemistry, as well as opportunities for interdisciplinary study with other sciences, materials science and engineering. Graduate students also have access to state-of-the-art instrumentation facilities in X-ray crystallography, mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance and electron microscopy. Our Ph.D. graduates are well prepared for careers in industry, government and academia.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Chemistry

description: The UNT doctoral program in Clinical Psychology provides broad-based training in clinical psychology with an emphasis on the integration of clinical science and practice. Our APA-accredited Ph.D. program in Clinical Psychology is a generalist program that emphasizes research and clinical training in a broad range of areas within clinical psychology. These include: child, adolescent and family psychology; clinical neuropsychology; health psychology; forensic psychology; and schizophrenia/schizotypy. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the necessary knowledge, skills and experience for entry-level professional practice as a licensed psychologist.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA)
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Clinical Psychology

description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Computer Science and Engineering at the University of North Texas is a research-intensive degree designed to produce highly qualified individuals capable of making significant contributions to the field of computer science and engineering. The program emphasizes deep theoretical understanding, advanced research methodologies, and practical application, preparing students for leadership roles in academia, industry, and government research institutions.
Students in the CSE PhD program will engage in cutting-edge research across a wide array of areas, including but not limited to: artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, cybersecurity, software engineering, computer networks, computer architecture, bioinformatics, and robotics. The program fosters a collaborative environment where students work closely with faculty mentors on innovative projects, contribute to scientific literature, and present their findings at national and international conferences. Graduates are equipped with the skills to conduct independent research, develop new technologies, and contribute to the advancement of knowledge in computer science and engineering.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Computer Science and Engineering

description: The UNT Ph.D. in Counseling Psychology program emphasizes an ecological and multicultural perspective in its training of counseling psychologists. We prepare students for careers as counseling psychologists in academic settings (e.g., faculty positions), hospitals and medical settings, university counseling centers, community mental health centers, forensic settings, and independent practice. The program is committed to training psychologists who are competent in both research and practice and who can integrate these two areas of competence. The program emphasizes the importance of multicultural humility, social justice, and awareness of intersectionality. We seek to provide rigorous training in scientific research and evidence-based practice within a supportive and collaborative environment. This combination prepares our graduates to be effective and ethical practitioners, researchers, and educators in a diverse and global society.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of the American Psychological Association (APA). Our accreditation was reaffirmed in October 2021 for the next 7 years, with the next site visit scheduled for 2028.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Counseling Psychology

description: The Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision program prepares graduates to assume positions as counselor educators, supervisors, researchers, and advanced practitioners in academic and agency settings. The program is committed to developing leaders in the counseling profession who are highly competent in the areas of counseling, supervision, teaching, research and scholarship, leadership, and advocacy. Graduates are prepared for careers at the university level as faculty members who teach and supervise master’s and doctoral students, conduct research, and provide service to the profession. In addition, graduates are prepared to be supervisors and leaders in clinical settings.
Accreditation status: The doctoral program in Counselor Education and Supervision is accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) through March 31, 2028.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Counselor Education and Supervision

Concentration name: ESL Education, Early Childhood Education, Educational Technology, Elementary Education, Literacy, Mathematics Education, Research, Science Education, Social Studies Education, Special Education, STEM Education, Teacher Education
description: UNT’s Ph.D. in Curriculum and Instruction develops leaders, educators, scholars, and researchers who can make significant contributions to the field of curriculum and instruction in various contexts. In this program, students develop expertise in a specialization (e.g., literacy, mathematics education, science education, educational technology, early childhood education, teacher education, etc.) while also gaining a deep understanding of philosophical, historical, and sociological perspectives of curriculum, teaching, and learning. Students explore issues relevant to curriculum and instruction, conduct original research, and disseminate knowledge through presentation and publication. This program helps students develop the knowledge and skills necessary to prepare them for leadership roles in various educational settings, including higher education, schools, and professional organizations.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Curriculum and Instruction

description: The Ph.D. in Educational Leadership at the University of North Texas is designed to prepare reflective practitioners, researchers and scholars for leadership positions in higher education or K-12 school districts. This doctoral program requires a minimum of 66 post-master’s semester hours, including a dissertation. The program culminates in a dissertation on an original research project that contributes to the knowledge base of educational leadership. Graduates are prepared for careers as researchers, professors, policy analysts, administrators and leaders in academic, K-12 and other organizational settings. This program is offered by the Department of Educational Psychology.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Leadership

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program in Educational Psychology prepares students for positions as university faculty members, researchers and applied specialists in a variety of educational and research settings. The program places an emphasis on the acquisition of knowledge of human development, learning, motivation, cognition, measurement, and statistics. Through coursework and individually supervised research, students develop the skills necessary to analyze and synthesize existing research, conduct original research, and apply educational psychology principles to a range of practical settings. Students select a faculty mentor with shared research interests. Together, the student and mentor develop a plan of study that reflects the student's individual research interests and career goals. Students graduate with a strong theoretical understanding of educational psychology and the research skills necessary to pursue their individual research agendas.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Psychology

description: The Learning Sciences Ph.D. program in the Department of Educational Psychology at UNT is a highly interdisciplinary program focused on understanding and improving learning in a wide variety of contexts. Our program emphasizes design-based research, where students work closely with faculty mentors to design, implement, and evaluate innovative learning environments and interventions. Students will develop a deep understanding of learning theories, research methodologies, and instructional design principles, preparing them for careers as researchers, educators, and learning designers in academia, industry, and government settings.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Educational Psychology with a concentration in Learning Sciences

description: Electrical Engineering Ph.D. prepares students for leadership positions in research, development, and advanced engineering in industry, academia and government. Graduates are prepared to apply knowledge and contribute to the rapidly changing world of technology. The research interests of the faculty are diverse and encompass virtually every area of electrical engineering. We provide a stimulating environment for graduate studies and research. The Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering offers specializations in Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design, Communication Systems, Computer Vision and Machine Learning, Cyber-Physical Systems, Electromagnetics, Energy and Power Systems, Micro and Nanoelectronics, Signal and Image Processing, and Solid State and Optics.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical Engineering

description: The Department of Electrical Engineering offers a doctoral program leading to the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Electrical Engineering. The program is designed to provide students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary for careers in research, academia, and industry. Students will engage in cutting-edge research under the guidance of experienced faculty members, contributing to advancements in various fields of electrical engineering. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, preparing graduates to tackle complex engineering challenges and innovate in their respective areas of expertise. Graduates of the Ph.D. program will be equipped to assume leadership roles, conduct independent research, and make significant contributions to the field of electrical engineering.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical Engineering with a concentration in Biomedical Engineering

Concentration name: literary and cultural studies, rhetoric and composition, technical communication, creative writing
description: The PhD in English program provides advanced study in English, with specialization possible in literary and cultural studies, rhetoric and composition, technical communication, and creative writing. Students develop sophisticated research, analytical, and communication skills suitable for careers in academia, professional writing, and related fields. The program emphasizes scholarly inquiry, critical thinking, and original contribution to the field of English studies. The doctoral degree in English is designed to offer a balance between historical and theoretical approaches to literary, linguistic, and rhetorical studies, while also providing the opportunity to study and practice creative writing and technical communication. The program aims to prepare students for careers as university faculty, independent scholars, writers, editors, and researchers in various professional fields.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in English

description: The Ph.D. in Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a broad and comprehensive education in environmental science. The program emphasizes advanced knowledge of environmental systems and processes, the development and application of quantitative skills, and the critical evaluation of environmental issues and solutions. Students will conduct original research that contributes to the scientific understanding of environmental problems and their solutions. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, government, industry, and non-profit organizations where advanced expertise in environmental science is required.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science

description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Science is a multidisciplinary program designed for students seeking advanced training in the scientific foundations of environmental analysis and problem-solving. This program provides students with the opportunity to conduct independent, original research under the mentorship of faculty, contributing to the advancement of environmental knowledge. Students will specialize in one of seven concentrations, allowing for focused study in their area of interest. The Ph.D. program emphasizes critical thinking, research methodology, data analysis, and scientific communication, preparing graduates for leadership roles in academia, government, industry, and non-profit organizations. The Ecology and Conservation Biology concentration focuses on the study of interactions among organisms and their environment, biodiversity, ecological processes, and the conservation of natural resources. Students will explore topics such as population dynamics, community ecology, ecosystem function, landscape ecology, and conservation genetics, preparing them for careers in research, wildlife management, habitat restoration, and environmental policy.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Ecology and Conservation Biology

description: The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Environmental Science. This degree program prepares students for careers as scientists in academia, industry, or government agencies. Students completing the degree program will have the knowledge and skills necessary to address complex environmental problems using an integrative scientific approach. Students are able to pursue a concentration in Geoscience as part of this program.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Geoscience

description: The Environmental Science Ph.D. program is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers addressing complex environmental issues. Students will receive training in both theory and application of environmental science. Research areas include environmental assessment, ecology, toxicology, environmental chemistry, conservation, water quality, microbiology and human ecology. The Ph.D. program prepares students for careers in academia, environmental consulting and government agencies. Students are trained to become independent researchers and effective communicators of their research. Graduates from our program have been very successful in securing highly desirable positions. Our graduates are employed in faculty positions at universities, as research scientists in government agencies (e.g., USEPA), and as consultants in the private sector.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Human Ecology

description: The PhD in Environmental Science offers research-based doctoral training for students interested in careers addressing complex environmental issues. Students develop an interdisciplinary research program that emphasizes quantitative skills and a strong disciplinary foundation in a focus area within environmental science. This allows our students to pursue research at the interface of basic and applied science while addressing environmental problems. The program prepares students to become leading scientists and professionals in governmental agencies, environmental consulting firms, non-governmental organizations, industry, and academia. The PhD program will provide you with an interdisciplinary approach to environmental issues, cutting-edge research skills in your concentration area, and the ability to think critically and solve complex environmental problems.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Science Education Research

description:
The Department of Biological Sciences offers a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree in Environmental Science with a concentration in Toxicology. This doctoral program requires a minimum of 60 credit hours beyond the master’s degree, or 90 credit hours beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students entering with a master’s degree may transfer up to 30 hours of graduate coursework, provided the coursework is appropriate for the degree and was completed within the previous seven years.
The PhD program in Environmental Science is designed to prepare graduates for positions in academic, industrial, or governmental organizations. The curriculum provides students with a broad and fundamental knowledge of current concepts in environmental science. The PhD degree emphasizes scientific research and allows students to specialize in a particular area of environmental science, such as toxicology, ecology, environmental chemistry, or others. Students are expected to complete their dissertation research, pass the qualifying exam, and successfully defend their dissertation during their course of study.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Environmental Science with a concentration in Toxicology

description: The PhD in Health Sciences is an interdisciplinary doctoral degree that prepares students for academic, research and leadership positions in health sciences. The program offers a broad base of didactic knowledge and opportunities for applied research related to the complex issues in health sciences. The program will advance the student’s knowledge, research and leadership skills to address current and emerging public health issues. The doctoral program provides a didactic foundation in critical thinking, research methods and statistics, and epidemiology and public health. Students in the program will be able to apply theory to practice; design and conduct applied research and evaluation; analyze, interpret and disseminate research findings; and communicate health sciences related information to diverse audiences. The PhD in Health Sciences will prepare students for leadership roles to address the needs of public health and healthcare organizations and agencies, governmental entities and private industry.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Health Sciences

description: The Ph.D. in Higher Education at the University of North Texas is designed to prepare individuals for leadership, teaching, and research positions in colleges and universities, as well as positions with state and federal agencies and organizations related to postsecondary education. Graduates of the program are prepared to serve as administrators in a variety of postsecondary settings; as faculty in master’s-level higher education and student affairs programs; and as researchers/analysts in institutional research and policy settings. The program emphasizes the development of research and scholarship skills, and provides students with a broad understanding of the historical, philosophical, political, social, cultural, and economic foundations of higher education, as well as the organizational and leadership dimensions of colleges and universities. Areas of study include, but are not limited to, student affairs administration, college teaching, higher education management, higher education finance, higher education law, and the history and philosophy of higher education. The program also offers opportunities for individualized study through electives, independent studies, and dissertation research. The Ph.D. in Higher Education requires a minimum of 66 semester hours beyond the master’s degree, including 15 hours of core courses, 15 hours of research courses, 15 hours of electives, and 21 hours of dissertation. All students complete a doctoral qualifying examination prior to beginning dissertation work. All degree requirements must be completed within a period of 10 years.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Higher Education

description: Liberty University’s Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in History provides the advanced study and research skills needed to excel in the field of history. Our doctoral degree in history is designed to prepare graduates to conduct original research, critically evaluate historical interpretations, and teach at the university level. With the online history PhD program, you can advance your career as an educator, researcher, or historian. This PhD in history degree will provide you with the training you need to master the art of historiography, historical research, and historical writing. Through the study of a particular research topic or field, you can add to the body of historical knowledge while helping others learn more about the past. Our PhD in history online program offers an in-depth study of history. You can gain extensive knowledge of historical literature, theory, and research methodologies. In our Doctor of Philosophy in history program, you can sharpen your critical thinking and communication skills, while learning how to conduct original historical research and contribute to the field of history. With courses on historiography and historical methods, you can gain knowledge of the major themes and issues in various fields of history. This program will also help you master the art of teaching history at the university level. We are committed to training scholars who are prepared to make significant contributions to the field of history.
Accreditation status: Liberty University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges to award associate, bachelor’s, master’s, specialist, and doctoral degrees.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in History

description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree in Human Performance and Movement Science prepares students for careers as researchers and university faculty. The program is specifically designed to provide students with advanced theoretical knowledge related to human performance, research skills necessary to pursue an independent research agenda, and pedagogical skills needed for effective teaching in higher education.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Human Performance and Movement Science

description: The Department of Linguistics offers a concentration in Linguistics for the PhD in Information Science program at the University of North Texas. The doctoral program prepares students to become future researchers and faculty members in the field of information science, specializing in areas related to linguistics, language, and technology. Students in the Information Science PhD program, Linguistics Concentration, develop skills to analyze language data, conduct research using computational and theoretical approaches, and contribute to the interdisciplinary field of information science. The program emphasizes advanced theoretical knowledge, research methodologies, and practical applications in areas such as natural language processing, corpus linguistics, computational linguistics, and sociolinguistics. Students will work closely with faculty mentors on cutting-edge research projects, preparing them for careers in academia, industry, and government.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science

description: The Ph.D. in Information Science program prepares students for leadership positions as researchers, teachers, and professionals in academic, governmental, and commercial institutions. Students develop advanced knowledge of theoretical and conceptual foundations of information science, as well as proficiency in research methods. The program fosters critical and creative thinking, ethical reasoning, problem-solving, and effective communication skills.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Consumer Insights (Consumer Analytics)

description: The PhD in Information Science with a concentration in Cybersecurity is a doctoral program within the Department of Information Science at the University of North Texas. This program provides students with a strong theoretical foundation, advanced research skills, and specialized knowledge in cybersecurity, preparing them for leadership roles in academia, government, and industry. Students will engage in rigorous coursework and conduct original research under the guidance of expert faculty, contributing to the advancement of cybersecurity knowledge and practice. Graduates will be equipped to address complex cybersecurity challenges, innovate new solutions, and educate the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Cybersecurity

description: The PhD in Information Science with a concentration in Data Science provides students with advanced knowledge and skills in both theoretical and applied aspects of information science and data science. Students will engage in rigorous research, contribute to the body of knowledge in the field, and prepare for careers in academia, industry, or government. The program emphasizes interdisciplinary approaches, critical thinking, and advanced research methodologies to address complex data challenges.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Data Science

description: The Geospatial Information Science (GIS) concentration focuses on the theory and practice of geospatial information. It provides students with comprehensive knowledge and advanced research skills for addressing the challenges of our geospatial world. The GIS concentration is designed for students interested in a research-intensive degree and a career involving research and development in GIScience (e.g., academia, industry, or government). Students will gain advanced knowledge in geospatial data modeling, analysis, visualization, and application development.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Geospatial Information Science

description: The Ph.D. in Information Science program prepares students for careers in research, academia, and professional leadership roles. The program is designed to develop scholars who can conduct original research, contribute to the theoretical and applied knowledge base of the information science discipline, and educate future generations of information professionals. Students develop advanced research skills, learn to analyze complex information problems, and contribute to the evolution of information science. Graduates are prepared to advance knowledge and practice in various information-intensive environments.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Health Informatics

description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Information Science prepares students to conduct original research, teach at the university level and serve in a variety of leadership roles. Our program is distinctive for its interdisciplinary approach and for the emphasis it places on developing scholars who understand the societal impact of information in its many forms. Students completing the PhD program will be prepared to take an active role in shaping the future of information science.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Journalism

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Information Science provides doctoral students with opportunities to acquire in-depth knowledge of information science as a discipline and prepare for careers in research, teaching, or advanced professional positions. Our graduates are well-prepared for faculty positions, leadership roles in library and information science, or industry research and development.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Knowledge Management

description: The Ph.D. in Information Science program is designed for students seeking careers in teaching and research, and as leaders in the information professions. The program is a research-oriented, interdisciplinary program that leads to a doctoral degree in information science. It prepares highly skilled researchers who are able to apply theoretical knowledge and research methods to address challenges related to information organization, access, retrieval, use, preservation and education. Concentrations are available in Archives and Records Management, Bioinformatics, Computational Linguistics, Data Science, Health Informatics, Information Systems, Librarianship and Linguistics.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Information Science with a concentration in Linguistics

description: The Learning Technologies Ph.D. program prepares students for leadership and research positions in academic, corporate and government settings. Students learn how to apply theories of learning, instruction, and technology to the analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation of learning experiences. The program emphasizes advanced research skills in both quantitative and qualitative methods, providing students with the expertise to contribute to the field through scholarly publication, grant writing, and professional presentations.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Learning Technologies

description: The Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering is a research-oriented degree program tailored for students seeking a deeper understanding of the synthesis, structure, properties, and performance of materials, as well as their application in various technologies. The program is designed to equip graduates with advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, preparing them for leadership roles in academia, industry, and government research institutions. Our faculty members are at the forefront of materials research, offering expertise across a wide range of specialties. Students benefit from access to state-of-the-art facilities and opportunities to engage in groundbreaking projects. The curriculum emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration and innovative thinking, fostering an environment where students can develop novel materials and explore their potential applications.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Materials Science and Engineering prepares students for careers in industry, national laboratories, and academia. The program has extensive research activities across several areas including Biomaterials, Computational Materials Science, Electronic/Photonic Materials, Functional Materials, Nanomaterials, and Structural Materials. The program emphasizes a broad materials science and engineering background combined with in-depth knowledge in a specialization area.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science and Engineering with a concentration in Biomedical Engineering

description: The PhD in Materials Science and Engineering is an interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers in research, academia, and industry. The program emphasizes a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of materials science and engineering, with a focus on advanced materials characterization, processing, and computational modeling. Students will have opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research in various areas, including but not limited to advanced structural materials, functional materials, nanomaterials, biomaterials, and energy materials. The concentration in Mechanical and Energy Engineering allows students to specialize in topics such as advanced manufacturing, materials for extreme environments, energy storage and conversion materials, and mechanical behavior of materials. Graduates will be equipped with the knowledge and skills necessary to contribute to innovative solutions in materials-related fields. The program fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and effective communication skills, essential for leadership roles in materials science and engineering.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Materials Science and Engineering with a concentration in Mechanical and Energy Engineering

description: Mathematics can be considered the language of science and engineering. A Ph.D. in Mathematics at UNT prepares students to conduct original research in mathematics and apply advanced mathematical concepts to problems in science, engineering and other fields. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in core areas of mathematics and the opportunity to specialize in one or more areas of research. Students work closely with faculty mentors, engaging in cutting-edge research and contributing to the advancement of mathematical knowledge. Our graduates are well-prepared for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can utilize their expertise to solve complex problems and contribute to scientific and technological innovation.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Mathematics

Concentration name: Solid Mechanics, Thermofluid Systems, Energy Systems
description: The Doctor of Philosophy degree in Mechanical and Energy Engineering with concentrations in Solid Mechanics, Thermofluid Systems, or Energy Systems focuses on research and development of new mechanical and energy devices and systems. Students acquire specialized training in a research area leading to a dissertation. Students acquire advanced knowledge of the fundamental and applied aspects of mechanical and energy engineering, develop skills in analytical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental investigation, and conduct independent research that contributes to the advancement of knowledge in the field. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can apply their expertise to address complex engineering challenges and contribute to technological innovation.
Program name: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Mechanical and Energy Engineering

description: The Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Mechanical and Energy Engineering program emphasizes research in core areas of mechanical engineering as well as emerging areas related to energy engineering. The program prepares students for careers in academia, research, and industry. Our graduate students are involved in cutting-edge research in areas such as advanced materials, biomedical engineering, computational fluid dynamics, energy systems, manufacturing, and robotics.
